public_rationale: Anthropic's April 9, 2026 description presents agents as useful while acknowledging mistakes and the need for human input [e1]. Its September 18 disclosure reports a 76% success rate on its most open-ended internal engineering tasks in May 2026 [e2]. These reports do not compare a representative set of public promises with matching May performance, supervision requirements and net human time, so they establish neither general delivery nor material failure to deliver [e1][e2].
limitations: The April description is context, not a May performance evaluation [e1].
The May success figure is company-reported internal performance, without independent replication supplied here [e2].
The evidence does not establish whether advertised autonomy reduced total human effort under the promised conditions [e1][e2].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: AI does not deliver what it has been promised to tech workers.

statement.excerpt: AI does not do what you have been promised it does, and those who are excited about it are excited because they believe it will replace you.

from_speaker: AI does not do what you have been promised it does
our_interpretation: Assess the normalized proposition about capability delivery. The separate assertion about enthusiasts' motives is outside this listed proposition.
In context, the ordinary reading concerns agents doing useful tech work reliably with substantially less continuous prompting and supervision.
This is not interpreted as claiming that AI performs no useful tasks.
Use May 2026, the latest completed month before the June 30 post, for the ongoing capability observation. Earlier promises may provide context, but performance evidence must describe this period.
No particular product, promise, task distribution, or acceptable failure rate is supplied.
criteria.support_condition: A representative comparison of public promises with reproducible May 2026 performance shows a material failure to deliver the advertised autonomy and reduction in human effort.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable evidence shows that the advertised autonomy and reduction in human effort were generally delivered under the promised conditions.

evidence.excerpt: But the autonomy that makes agents useful also introduces a range of new risks.
evidence.locator: Opening discussion of agent capabilities and risks
evidence.explanation: Anthropic presents useful agent autonomy while explicitly acknowledging mistakes and human control. A promise-versus-performance test must preserve those qualifications rather than assume a promise of unattended perfection.

evidence.excerpt: Claude’s success rate reached 76% in May 2026
evidence.locator: Discussion of Claude's success on open-ended internal engineering tasks
evidence.explanation: The page reports substantial success alongside incomplete reliability in the target month. Its internally selected tasks and company-defined success measure do not settle delivery against the broader, unspecified promises; the read version carries a September 18 update.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A representative, reproducible comparison of specific public promises with May 2026 performance, matching product versions, tasks and operating conditions. It must measure success, human intervention and net human time to establish whether the promised autonomy and effort reductions were generally delivered or materially fell short.
